scope: Windows 2025 source build and actual Host contracts; no installer or native GUI claim.

runs.cause: Windows readlink uses native backslashes; detailed follow-up 83beaa3b isolated one ACP link.

failures: Missing app-boot was correctly rejected, but the assertion matched only POSIX package separators.
pnpm add wrote a portable link specifier, while the assertion expected native Windows backslashes.

runs.result: failed actual SDK target after removing another plugin
runs.failure: After the path representation assertions passed, pnpm remove restored the old-youdub-plugin target despite the updated dependency specifier. The existing realpath assertion correctly caught the behavior.

corrections.production: Source inventory and staging compare portable link targets; preserve file bytes, Git executable modes and POSIX backslashes. Profile preparation now writes portable pnpm link specifiers instead of Windows native backslashes.
corrections.tests: Normalize native separators when checking missing-module paths and equivalent pnpm link destinations; retain original cause, dependency identity, realpath, user-data and uninstall assertions. The migration regression also resolves the lockfile version to the actual SDK target before remove; post-remove realpath assertions remain.

nextRun.purpose: Verify portable link specifiers fix the actual Windows stale SDK target.

limitations: The full Windows job is not yet green.
